title: Types, arithmetic and comparison: a total and three bands
summary: Keep a running total in an INT variable, add to it on each press, and turn it into three BOOL results with comparison operators.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish the range of a real sensor or the overflow behaviour of a particular controller, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Use an INT variable for a number and a BOOL variable for a yes or no, and see that a comparison turns a number into a BOOL.
Add to a number only on the rising edge of an input, so that a button held for several scans counts once.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/TypedSteps.st the INT variable Total and the comparisons Low (Total < 10), Exact (Total = 10) and High (Total > 10) are written. Write the arithmetic: on each rising edge of Step add 5 to Total, and while Reset is TRUE set Total to 0.
stages.checkpoint: Total goes 0, 5, 10, 15, and the three outputs show which band it is in.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Step is pressed three times, the first press lasting two scans. Predict which output is ON at {{t:20}}, {{t:40}} and {{t:60}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TypedSteps.Low=true,TypedSteps.Exact=false,TypedSteps.High=false@20|Low}} at {{t:20}} ms (Total is 5); {{v:TypedSteps.Low=false,TypedSteps.Exact=true,TypedSteps.High=false@40|Exact}} at {{t:40}} ms (Total is 10); {{v:TypedSteps.Low=false,TypedSteps.Exact=false,TypedSteps.High=true@60|High}} at {{t:60}} ms (Total is 15).

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter declares Total and the three comparisons but never changes Total, so Low stays ON for ever; add 5 to Total on each rising edge of Step and clear it while Reset is TRUE.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. Studio runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named TypedSteps and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:20}}, {{t:40}} and {{t:60}} ms: exactly one of the three outputs is ON each time, and Reset at {{t:80}} ms brings Low back.
stages.checkpoint: Exact is ON only at the one total of 10, from {{t:40}} ms; the long first press added 5 once, not twice.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: What happens if you write Exact as Total >= 10? And if you add 5 on every scan while Step is TRUE? Try each and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: A comparison gives a BOOL, and = is not the same as >=. The scenario only watches the three BOOL outputs; it does not show the value of Total itself or what happens when an INT overflows.

hints.text: Total is an INT, so Total + 5 is an INT. A rising edge is Step TRUE now and StepWas FALSE on the previous scan.
IF Reset THEN Total := 0; ELSIF Step AND NOT StepWas THEN Total := Total + 5; END_IF; StepWas := Step; Put it before the three comparison lines.

faultCases: The starter declares Total and the three comparisons but never changes Total, so Low stays ON for ever; add 5 to Total on each rising edge of Step and clear it while Reset is TRUE.
